newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Airline starts direct London-Kilimanjaro flights.
newsitem.headline: Airline starts direct London-Kilimanjaro flights.

text.p: Alliance Air, jointly owned by Uganda, Tanzania and South Africa, has inaugurated direct flights to London and Kilimanjaro airport in northern Tanzania.
An Alliance Air Boeing 747 with more than 100 passengers aboard landed at Kilimanjaro airport on Monday en route to London from Johannesburg at the start of a new weekly service.
Johan Bosman, Tanzania manager for Alliance, said the new service was aimed at European tourists who previously were forced to use the Kenyan capital Nairobi for access to northern Tanzania.
The northern Tanzanian circuit includes famous attractions such as the Serengeti wildlife reserve, the Ngorongoro conservation area and Mount Kilimanjaro national park.
On Friday, Tanzanian Tourism Minister Zakia Meghji said tourism earned a record $322 million from 326,194 visitors in 1996. Tanzania's goal is to attract 500,000 tourists per year by the year 2000.

Alliance, in its third year of operation, is owned by the Tanzanian and Ugandan governments with 30 percent each and South African Airlines SAA.CN with 40 percent. Its headquarters are in Kampala, Uganda.
